newsitem.title: UK: AMEC says 1996 in line, plans asset sale.
newsitem.headline: AMEC says 1996 in line, plans asset sale.

text.p: Construction and engineering group AMEC Plc said on Thursday that group trading in 1996 had been in line with its expectations.
It said that following a strategic review of long-term land holdings of its housing subsidiary Fairclough Homes, it had decided to accelerate the sale of of some of its assets.
As a result of this, AMEC said it would be reducing the carrying value of assets of Fairclough Homes and related companies by 25 million stg.
It said the adjustment in carrying values would be reflected in its 1996 results as an exceptional item.
"This adjustment in carrying values anticipates the prospective level of proceeds from the planned realisation of current assets," the company said in a statement.

AMEC has already said its results for the year ending December 31, 1996 would include an exceptional profit of 31.6 million stg on the sale of its 50 percent stake in Building and Property Management Services Ltd (BPMS).
The company also announced on Thursday it had appointed Richard Fraser as chief executive of Fairclough Homes.
